findings.title: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process is always False for spawn processes, so hung flushers are never killed
findings.body: `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is never true for the processes this class creates. The flusher uses `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, whose `Process` class is `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` — a sibling of `multiprocessing.Process` (which is the fork-context flavor), not a subclass of it. The type annotation on `self.processes` (`SpawnProcess | threading.Thread`) even acknowledges this. Consequences: (1) In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a flusher process is deemed unhealthy due to a hang, `process.kill()` is silently skipped before the replacement process is started — previously the kill was unconditional, so this is a regression. The hung process keeps running indefinitely: it keeps flushing the same shards as its replacement, and because the restart reuses the same shared `healthy_since` Value for that process slot, a still-looping zombie can keep refreshing `healthy_since` and permanently mask the hang from the health check. (2) The same wrong check at line 346 means `join()` never calls `terminate()` on spawn processes that outlive the deadline. Fix by checking `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` or by calling `kill()`/`terminate()` unconditionally as before.

findings.title: Unset max_processes defaults to one process per shard instead of preserving old single-process behavior
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` makes an unset value mean "one process per shard", the most aggressive setting. The new `--flusher-processes` click option defaults to 1, which preserves the previous single-flusher-process behavior, but any construction path that does not pass the new parameter gets the aggressive behavior: for example an ops override of the `process-spans` entry in `SENTRY_KAFKA_CONSUMERS` that still uses the old `click_options` shape (the ops repo is deployed independently of this code), or any direct Python instantiation of `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory`/`SpanFlusher`. Such deployments would silently go from 1 flusher process to N spawned processes and N Kafka producers per consumer on upgrade, contrary to the PR's stated gradual-rollout intent. The default for `flusher_processes=None` should be 1, with per-shard scaling opt-in via the option.

findings.title: --flusher-processes is not validated; 0 is silently treated as per-shard and a negative value crashes startup with KeyError
findings.body: The new `--flusher-processes` option (and `SpanFlusher`'s `max_processes`) accepts any integer without validation. Passing 0 is silently treated as "one process per shard" because `0 or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` takes the shard count. Passing a negative number is worse: `self.num_processes = min(-1, len(shards))` is negative, so `process_to_shards_map` is built from `range(-1)` and is empty, and the very first shard assignment `self.process_to_shards_map[0].append(shard)` raises a bare `KeyError`, crashing the consumer at startup with no useful message. The option should be validated as `>= 1` (in the click callback or the constructor) and 0 should either be rejected or documented.

findings.title: Inconsistent metrics tag keys: "shard" vs "shards", and comma-joined multi-shard tag values
findings.body: The new per-process metrics tagging is inconsistent: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185) and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` (line 196) are tagged with key `"shard"`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` (line 199) uses key `"shards"`, so dashboards or monitors grouping/filtering by `shard` will silently miss the wait_produce timer. Additionally, when `max_processes < len(assigned_shards)` a process handles multiple shards and the tag value is a comma-joined list like "0,2,4", whereas `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` (line 243) emits one data point per individual shard integer — two different conventions for the same dimension that cannot be correlated in metrics queries.

findings.title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep
findings.body: `test_basic` monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op at the top of the test (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`), so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` with the comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change" provides no synchronization whatsoever. The test still depends on the racing flusher thread observing `current_drift.value = 9000` and completing a flush+produce before `step.join()` sets `stopped.value`; if the flusher thread's next loop iteration starts after `stopped` is set, it exits without flushing and `(msg,) = messages` fails on an empty list. If the intent was to deflake the test, this doesn't do it — the flusher's completion needs to be awaited deterministically (e.g., poll `messages` with a real timeout loop, since the fake sleep also makes the flusher's own `time.sleep(1)` a hot spin).

findings.title: Dead method _create_process_for_shard left over from per-shard design
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is never called anywhere: the restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. This leftover single-shard helper is misleading (it suggests per-shard restarts are possible when a restart actually recreates the whole multi-shard process) and should be removed.
